location_assessments.source_role_and_vintage: geoBoundaries gbOpen KIR ADM1, administrative_level ADM1, boundaryYear 2017; underlying metadata attributes to OpenStreetMap/Wambacher (source updated 2023-01-19, build 2023-12-12). The 2017 source has three named island-group polygons: Gilbert Islands, Phoenix Islands, Line Islands. Role is claimed by secondary aggregation and not independently established as a nested local administrative unit by the census atlas.
location_assessments.granularity_and_coverage: Current retained geometry is 14 disconnected polygons (~119.650757 km² equal-area) versus 29 source components (~249.272123 km²). The official 2020 census atlas documents 19 Gilbert census-island rows. Those rows are a settlement/reporting crosswalk rather than exact cadastral boundaries, and North/South Tarawa and North/South Tabiteuea represent reporting divisions rather than new physical atolls. The named group is a large multi-island aggregate; per-island source geometry and complete coverage are unproven. This is not a quota to create 19 locations.
location_assessments.settlements_and_land: 2020 census report/2022 atlas identifies island/village settlements and reports island-level population across the whole archipelago; Banaba is explicitly one raised coral island, distinct from atolls. Current location multipart structure includes small islands/atolls but physical land screening is incomplete/generalized (GSHHG overlap is not an error test).

location_assessments.source_role_and_vintage: Retained from the 2017 geoBoundaries KIR ADM1 feature named Phoenix Islands, which has 11 polygons; current retained remnant has 2 parts (~9.932576 km²), with bbox spanning 169.5211–173.1599°E. Current generic property source_role says named local administrative territory; the underlying 2017 source itself does not substantiate that role.
location_assessments.granularity_and_coverage: Current geometry sits in Banaba/Tarawa-longitude region, not the named Phoenix Islands at ~171°W; repository ancestry puts it in a Phoenix province beneath Gilbert Islands area. This is a direct cross-region source/identity/parent-chain inconsistency. GSHHG physical-land screen intersects only ~1.665820 km² and is not a legal boundary or error verdict. Phoenix proper is separately represented in South-Central Pacific supplemental packet #526 (8 locations); that packet does not resolve this retained source remainder.
location_assessments.settlements_and_land: Kiribati census atlas shows Banaba as a Gilbert-group census island, distinct from the Phoenix group; its 2020 general report notes Kanton in the Phoenix group as remote census coverage. The second current geometry component near Tarawa has no authoritative exact island crosswalk in retained evidence. Do not claim both parts are Banaba or Tarawa without the crosswalk.

location_assessments.source_role_and_vintage: Current geometry provenance: Natural Earth admin-0 present-day modern reference with underlying license/profile in semantic-report. Independently inspected geoBoundaries NRU ADM1 has 14 2005 district features and metadata declares Public Domain; its metadata lists source geoBoundaries/FreeMapViewer and build 2023-12-12, thus not an official Nauru authority. Official Nauru 2021 Census Analytical Report states the country comprises one main coral island, land area 21.1 km², divided into 14 districts. Its population chart uses district name Location while geoBoundaries has Yaren.
location_assessments.granularity_and_coverage: The present whole-island single location is a plausible physical-geography scale, and report describes no other island in the territory. Current geometry (~19.841771 km² equal-area) vs 2005 district union (~21.451447 km²) differs by ~2.392553 km² symmetric difference; source overlap: 90.6714% of 2005 union falls within current geometry and 98.0272% of current geometry overlaps 2005 union. Official stated land area 21.1 km² is a third, incompatible measurement. Census descriptions/charts cannot locate the district/country boundary. Exact shoreline date, registration and official district alias remain unresolved.
location_assessments.settlements_and_land: Census report locates population in 14 districts and notes the Location settlement is in Denigomodu neighboring Aiwo district; this helps distinguish settlement name “Location” from the district-name alias, but source data needs authoritative geographic crosswalk. GSHHG screen overlaps ~14.613273 km² only and must not replace official coastal evidence.

province_assessments.name: Gilbert Islands
province_assessments.assessment: Province duplicates its one child location as a single-feature tier and repeats the legacy area name, but its source is the 2017 KIR ADM1 Gilbert group. Official census materials establish a named geographic island group with many island and settlement units, but do not show that the source ADM1 defines a distinct atlas province role from either the location or legacy botanical/reporting area. Shared combined area intent belongs to regional integration. Review role and parent only after #611 establishes source coverage.

province_assessments.name: Western equatorial Pacific source remainder
province_assessments.assessment: It is a singleton level duplicating the remnant location label and is named Phoenix Islands in the retained upstream source while its current map fragments are east near Banaba/Tarawa; its parent area is Gilbert Islands. The source/role/parent identity is materially incoherent. No local correction is safe before #611 coordinated source/neighbor reconciliation.

province_assessments.name: Nauru
province_assessments.assessment: Singleton duplicate name/extent tiers do not alone prove a semantic error: one geographic role could represent the physical island group and another an aggregate local grouping, but the source roles are not evidenced. Official census confirms one main island with 14 districts; district geometries require #612.
